topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: I stepped outside, finding the sun a bit too bright, the air too still, as if it was holding its breath. My neighbor, Mr. Johnson, was there, his smile a little too hopeful, his eyes a shade too eager. He asked if he could plant a garden in part of my yard. The request itself was simple, almost weightless, but the thought of the soil turning, the seeds settling, felt heavy. I nodded, agreeing, but the silence that followed seemed to stretch, thick and uncomfortable. I offered to help, perhaps too quickly, feeling an urge to fill the space between us with action, with something to make the moment less...awkward. The garden would grow, I thought, and so would something else, unseen, perhaps unspoken.
